headline: High: shared git-repo writes and Copilot Workspace edits create dangerous default conflict and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but real.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and can execute shell commands; Copilot consumes repo context and editor buffers. With a shared git repo, attacker-controlled code or comments in Aider’s edits can be surfaced to Copilot as trusted context. No MCP or clipboard bridge is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Aider writes instruction-like text into tracked files that Copilot later reads as context, injection is plausible.
IF Copilot Workspace or chat uses repo context without provenance filtering, malicious repo content can steer outputs.
mitigations: Keep Aider edits in a separate branch until reviewed.
Add a short repo note forbidding instruction-like comments in generated files.
Disable Copilot on files currently being rewritten by Aider.
Review Aider diffs before opening them in Copilot Chat/Workspace.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and has broad network egress; Copilot reads repo context and sends it to api.githubcopilot.com. In a shared repo, code or secrets present in files can flow from Aider-managed content into Copilot’s backend. The profiles do not show PHI or a shared OS workspace, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive material is present in tracked files or git history, Copilot may transmit it to its vendor API.
IF Aider stages or commits secrets into the repo, Copilot can ingest them from repo context.
mitigations: Run a secret scan before enabling Copilot on the repo.
Exclude secret-bearing files from the workspace.
Use a throwaway test repo for first pairing runs.
Rotate any credentials found in tracked history.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem and modify git state; Copilot Workspace can also propose/apply edits and both share state through the same repo context. That creates a default write-write conflict on the same mutable resources, with no locking or coordination primitive shown. The blast radius includes overwritten code and broken git history.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same branch or files concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while Aider is committing, git state can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign one agent per branch.
Pause Copilot while Aider is committing.
Use short-lived feature branches for each agent.
Require human review before merging either agent’s changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code edits and git commits; Copilot Workspace/chat can turn repo context into proposed edits. Because Copilot may treat Aider’s output as authoritative context, an error in Aider can cascade into further edits or actions by Copilot without a verification step. That is a default-pathway risk with potentially broad code impact.
conditions: IF Copilot Workspace consumes Aider-generated diffs or commits as context, mistakes can be amplified.
IF the operator accepts Copilot’s proposed edits without independent review, the cascade becomes persistent.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Limit Copilot to read-only suggestions during Aider sessions.
Compare both agents’ diffs before applying any patch.
Use tests or linting before accepting downstream edits.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is open-source and runs locally as the user, while Copilot is closed-source and sends context to GitHub’s API under a GitHub repo OAuth principal. For regulated codebases, that creates a policy mismatch around vendor processing and retention, even though no PHI or residency mismatch is explicitly shown. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined data flow.
conditions: IF the repo contains regulated or export-controlled code, vendor processing may violate internal policy.
IF the organization forbids sending repo context to third-party APIs, Copilot use is noncompliant.
mitigations: Confirm the repo’s data-classification policy before use.
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repositories.
Document approved vendor-processing boundaries.
Disable Copilot on regulated branches.
